seoTitle: Percentage Change Calculator - Increase or Decrease
metaDescription: Free online Percentage Change Calculator. Instantly determine if a number increased or decreased and by exactly what percentage.
intro: Tracking data over time? Our free Percentage Change Calculator automatically detects whether your data grew or shrank, providing the exact percentage change in an instant.
whatIs: The Percentage Change Calculator is a comprehensive mathematical tool that measures the relative shift from an old value to a new value. It automatically identifies if the shift is an increase or a decrease.
howToUse: Enter the historical (original/old) number in the first input.
Enter the current (new) number in the second input.
The tool calculates the shift, telling you exactly the percentage of increase or decrease.
howItWorks: The tool uses the standard formula: ((New Value - Old Value) / |Old Value|) × 100. If the final result is positive, it reports a percentage increase. If negative, it reports a percentage decrease.
workedExample: If a stock was $50 and is now $40: ((40 - 50) / 50) × 100 = (-10 / 50) × 100 = -20%. The tool reports this as a 20% Decrease.
resultInterpretation: The output tells you the exact momentum of your data. A positive change indicates growth, while a negative change indicates contraction or loss.
useCases: Stock Market: Tracking the daily or annual percentage shift of a specific stock ticker.
Retail Business: Comparing Q1 sales revenue against Q2 sales revenue.
Traffic Analytics: Understanding if website pageviews went up or down compared to last month.
tipsAndLimitations: This is the best all-in-one percentage tool to use if you are tracking data over time but don't know ahead of time if the numbers will go up or down.
If the old value is zero, percentage change is undefined (you cannot divide by zero).

faq.question: What is the difference between Percentage Change and Percentage Difference?
faq.answer: Percentage Change is used when one specific thing changes over time (Old vs New). Percentage Difference is used when comparing two separate things where neither is the 'original'.

faq.question: Can a percentage change be more than 100%?
faq.answer: Yes, but only for an increase. A 100% increase means the value doubled. However, a decrease cannot exceed 100% unless the value drops into negative numbers.

disclaimer: This tool requires a non-zero starting value. Calculations resulting in extremely long decimals will be rounded.
